text:
sara-cs: Hey @acme-infra we just noticed a sustained 429 spike for your production org starting ~2026-06-05 03:12 UTC. Customer reports ~30s bursts every few minutes, hitting RPM/TPM limits. Can you share any recent deploys or retry logic?

acme-infra: Yep we rolled a lambda change last hour that retries failed SQS messages. It accidentally removed a jitter/backoff. We're seeing a fanout when the visibility timeout kicks in.

elaine: Can you paste a sample response header from the 429s? We need the x-rw-* headers to confirm which limiter triggered.

acme-infra: Here's one from our logs (sanitized):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-type: rpm
x-rw-rate-limit-limit: 600
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 14
x-request-id: acme-req-8a7c
```

acme-infra: Pattern is: 600 req/min per org, then a hard cutoff for ~15s. After cut we see client retry loops that attempt many parallel requests.

tim-oncall: That looks like the RPM window. Two quick checks from our side: 1) are these requests coming from multiple source IPs/regions or a single region? 2) were any of our fallbacks triggered (model variant fallthrough)? I can pull the per-node token pools.

acme-infra: All from us in us-east-1, multiple Lambda instances. We also noticed many cold starts right before spikes, so some burst of concurrent workers.

raj: Quick mitigation suggestions: 1) add client-side token-bucket limiter (leaky bucket) scoped to org key; 2) add randomized jitter on retries; 3) collapse duplicate work if SQS redrives same event. Also consider lowering lambda concurrency for a short window.

elaine: From the platform side we can: - temporarily raise the RPM for this org for 30m if you need breathing room; - recommend Dedicated bursts if this is regular; - enable per-route smoothing for streaming endpoints. Which do you want? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

acme-infra: Please raise RPM by 2x for 30m while we patch. Also sharing a small repro so you can see the exact pattern: we replayed 1k SQS messages in 10s. Logs: `for id in $(seq 1 1000); do invoke-lambda --id $id & done` — our bad.

sara-cs: Done, raised to 1200 rpm for 30m. Sent notice to billing & ops. Add me to updates once you patch client.

tim-oncall: I pulled the per-node token metrics — we saw token pool exhaustion at 03:12:04 across 3 frontends, then a synchronized reset ~14s later which matches the header. No fallback model switches.

raj: Patch checklist for acme: 1) update lambda handler to use exponential backoff + jitter (eg base 100ms, cap 5s, jitter 0-100%), 2) use a shared token-bucket in your task layer (redis or in-memory with leaky behavior), 3) enable request collapsing on duplicate event ids, 4) add a short random delay on startup to avoid thundering cold starts.

acme-infra: Thanks — we'll push a fix in 20m and throttle concurrency in the meantime. Can you confirm what the proper retry semantics should be so our SDKs behave?

elaine: Recommend RFC-compliant Retry-After handling: treat 429 as retriable with exponential backoff + jitter. Respect X-RW-Rate-Limit-Reset when present: spread retries after reset window. Also prefer streaming when possible to avoid bursty request storms.

acme-infra: Pushing a patch now that adds jitter and a per-org token bucket in Redis. We'll monitor.

deploy-bot: deploy acme/retry-patch v1.2.3 to us-east-1 started by acme-ci at 03:28 UTC

sara-cs: Thanks, I flagged this as "resolved" for now. Please re-open if you see 429s after the patch. :thumbsup:

acme-infra: Patch went out, initial observations look good — no repeat 429s in the last 7m. We'll follow up after 24h. Appreciate the quick bump.

tim-oncall: I'll close the temporary RPM increase in 18m. If this recurs, we can schedule a deeper replay analysis (trace IDs appreciated).

sara-cs: Closing here — summary: root cause = lambda retry fanout + no jitter, symptom = org RPM exhausted, fix = client backoff + per-org token bucket, platform mitigation = temporary RPM raise.
